lēnōnĭus , a, um, adj. id.,
I.of or pertaining to pimping or pandering: non periclumst nequid recte monstres. Ba. Non lenoniumst (sc. recte monstrare), Plaut. Ps. 1, 3, 53: “aedes,” id. Truc. 1, 1, 30 ; id. Men. 3. 3, 29: “servitus,” id. Pers. 3, 1, 1 : “fides,” id. Rud. 5, 3, 30 : “genus,” id. Curc. 4, 2, 13 ; id. Pers. 4, 4, 33: “quoi servitutem di danunt lenoniam Puero,” id. Ps. 3, 1, 1 : pueri, Verr. Fl. Fragm. Fast. Praenest. ad VII. K. Maias (in Inscr. Orell. T. 2, p. 410): “lutum lenonium, as a term of reproach,” filthy pander, Plaut. Pers. 3, 3, 2 : “jam ego hoc ipsum oppidum expugnatum faxo erit lenonium,” i. e. will outwit this pander, id. Ps. 2, 4, 76 : “Juppiter lenonius,” id. ib. 1, 3, 99 .—Adv.: lēnōniē , v. lenonice.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
